scope: BBC versus eight pinned Brainfuck compilers on one Linux x86-64 host: 18 programs, build time, run time, executable size, peak RSS. BBC builds and runs Windows x86-64 under Wine 9.0; competitors build and run natively on Linux x86-64; brainfry also has a windows-x86_64 arm under Wine for a same-platform comparison.

method.trials: One validation build+run (also warmup), then 5 interleaved build trials and 5 run trials per arm and program, arm order rotated each trial. Medians per program; geometric means per group.
method.timing: Fresh process through a static C launcher (peakrss) measuring wall time from fork to wait.
method.memory: Peak RSS = maximum resident set of the largest process in the waited tree (RUSAGE_CHILDREN); includes the launcher floor of about 1.7 MiB.
method.correctness: stdout bytes and exit 0 compared with a reference interpreter output (sierpinski reference from brainfry bfinterp).
method.wine: Persistent wineserver (wineserver -p) for Wine arms, as a Windows host keeps its services running; cold-start samples retained.
limitations: Not Windows-native and not on a device; BBC timings include Wine process startup (about 43 ms).
Shared 4-core cloud host; occasional multi-second stalls possible.
pablojorge/brainfuck tape is 30,000 cells and not zero-initialized; it fails nested_math.

arms.brainfry-win (Wine): Windows x86-64 under Wine 9.0 (same platform as BBC)

results.wine_note: Wine arms (BBC, brainfry-win) were rerun with a persistent wineserver (wineserver -p), as a Windows host keeps its OS services running. The first run let wineserver exit during long Brainfly builds, so each Wine process paid a ~0.55 s cold start; those samples are kept under wine_cold_results.
